==Problem==

In January <imath>1980</imath> the Mauna Loa Observatory recorded carbon dioxide <imath>(CO2)</imath> levels of <imath>338</imath> ppm (parts per million). Over the years the average <imath>CO2</imath> reading has increased by about <imath>1.515</imath> ppm each year. What is the expected <imath>CO2</imath> level in ppm in January <imath>2030</imath>? Round your answer to the nearest integer. 

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 399\qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 414\qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 420\qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 444\qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 459</imath>

==Solution 1==

This is a time period of <imath>2030 - 1980 = 50</imath> years, so we can expect the ppm to increase by <imath>50*1.515=75.75\approx	76</imath> ppm.
Since we started with <imath>338</imath> ppm, we have <imath>76+338=\boxed{\textbf{(B)\ 414}}</imath>.

-ILoveMath31415926535
==Solution 2==
<imath>2030 - 1980 = 50</imath> years.
The ppm level in 2030 is <imath>338 + 50 * 1.515 = 338 + 75.75 = 413.75</imath> <imath>
\approx	\boxed{\textbf{(B)\ 414}}</imath>.
 
~thebanker88

==Solution 3==

From Jan 1980 =338 ppm increase

= 1.515 ppm increased / year

= 50 yrs (in this case)
=1.515 x 50 

=75.75 ~ 76

Thus, 2030 prediction = 338 + 76 = 414 = option B 
 
~ Runningmouse
